researched_by: user report from a visit (Fontburn), plus operator pages and user forums for the rest
policy_summary:
A company-wide scheme, not a site arrangement. Overnight parking is permitted and charged at reservoirs across the north east, with a shared booking system covering Balderhead, Derwent, Fontburn, Selset, Grassholme, Scaling Dam and Kielder. Typically GBP10 a night with no facilities - no hook-up, no waste disposal - and rangers check tickets in the evening.

This is the answer to whether water companies are a per-site or per-company research job. Per company. One operator, one scheme, seven reservoirs. If United Utilities and Yorkshire Water work the same way, the landowner tier is far smaller work than the councils.
notes: Kielder is the exception and needs care - see the Kielder note below. Elsewhere the pattern looks consistent: pay at the visitor centre or online, ranger checks in the evening, gates close overnight.
open_questions: Confirm the current price at each reservoir - GBP10 is reported at Fontburn and Derwent.
Which reservoirs have gates that lock, and at what time? Derwent reported as closing with reopening at 08:00.
Do other water companies run equivalent schemes? That decides the size of the whole landowner tier.

sites.payment_notes: Machine is not always on. Hut only when staffed. Online otherwise - and if there is no signal, payment can be settled the next day.
sites.notes: Confirmed by a regular visitor. The deferred payment arrangement is unusual and worth knowing - no signal does not prevent staying.

sites.name: Tower Knowe, Kielder Water
sites.search_hint: Tower Knowe Visitor Centre, Kielder Water
sites.notes: Advertised for motorhomes, campervans and caravans at GBP10 a night. BUT see the Kielder warning - visitor reports conflict sharply, with one party moved on by a ranger at 21:00 from Hawkhope after paying, and told overnight stays are not allowed anywhere at Kielder. Verify before relying on this.

sites.name: Other Kielder Water car parks (Hawkhope, South Abutment, Matthew's Linn, Bakethin)
sites.notes: CONFLICTING EVIDENCE. Some visitors report paying GBP10 for overnight at Hawkhope with a friendly ranger checking tickets; another was moved on at 21:00 and told overnight stays are not permitted anywhere at Kielder. Day parking is GBP5, transferable across car parks, with a stargazing option until 03:00 which is not the same as staying the night. Do not publish a verdict for these until checked directly.

kielder_note: Kielder Water & Forest Park is run by a development trust whose members include Northumbrian Water, the Forestry Commission, Northumberland County Council, Calvert Trust and Kielder Observatory. Responsibility therefore varies by car park: Kielder Castle is Forestry England's at GBP15, Tower Knowe is Northumbrian Water's at GBP10, and several others sit under the shared GBP5 day-parking scheme with unclear overnight status. A single destination with at least three regimes - and the strongest argument yet that the data model must key on the car park, never on the destination.
